title: Rule on Meter Installations Held at a Service Agreement (Metering Service)
content:
**Rule.** Under the **Metering Service**, each service agreement has one meter in service at a time. A customer may hold meter installations at every service agreement the customer has, and there is no limit on the number of installations one customer may hold across those agreements. The same agreement accumulates installations over time as meters are exchanged.

**One open order per agreement.** No other installation order for the same service agreement is in scheduled status. The company's installation records decide this, read for the service agreement named on the new order: where an order for that agreement already stands in scheduled status, a further order for the same agreement is not placed alongside it. An order for a different service agreement of the same customer is unaffected.

**Exchange.** An exchange is made by ordering the new meter while the old one is in service; the old meter is removed on the day the new one is installed.

## The rule in condition and result form

| Condition, read from the installation records | Result |
|---|---|
| The agreement has no installation order in scheduled status | A new installation order may be placed for that agreement |
| The agreement already has an installation order in scheduled status | No second order for the same agreement is placed |
| The agreement's current meter is in service and a new meter is ordered | The new meter is the exchange; the old meter is removed on the new meter's installation day |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A customer holds two agreements, one for a home and one for a shop. A scheduled order at the home agreement does not prevent an order at the shop agreement.
- An agreement's meter was exchanged twice over the years. The agreement now shows three installations: two removed and one in service; only the one in service is the meter in service.
